dedupe_keys.name: iwa benchmark simulation models bsm1 bsm1lt bsm2

description: The Benchmark Simulation Models are simulation environments for evaluating control strategies for activated sludge wastewater treatment plants. Each benchmark defines a plant layout, a process model, influent loads, test procedures and evaluation criteria, so that once a user has validated their simulation code any control strategy can be compared fairly. BSM1 is a five-compartment reactor with anoxic zone and secondary settler combining nitrification and predenitrification, evaluated over 14 days of dry, rainy and stormy weather; BSM1LT extends it to 609 days with faults such as toxic events and sensor and actuator failures; BSM2 adds sludge treatment with a primary settler, thickener, anaerobic digester and dewatering. Licence: not stated for the benchmark models; the WaterTAP implementation is BSD-3-Clause. Access is free of charge. They describe a generic municipal plant, not any real site. Implementations exist in several tools, including a steady-state BSM2 flowsheet in WaterTAP. Caveats: the page's BSM2 report is marked draft, and results depend on the implementation used. Simulation uses: optimisation and control design of treatment plants, capacity studies and testing digital-twin controllers against a shared reference. Related: WaterTAP (model-watertap).
